description: TCRP Research Report 226, An Update on Public Transportation's Impacts on Greenhouse Gas Emissions, by Jen McGraw and Peter Haas of the Center for Neighborhood Technology and Reid Ewing and Sadegh Sabouri of the University of Utah for the Transit Cooperative Research Program of the Transportation Research Board, gives an updated national analysis of public transportation's role as a climate solution by documenting its greenhouse gas impacts in 2018. Coverage: US public transport at national level, with a simple spreadsheet tool that provides the 2018 GHG impact findings by transit agency and lets users apply future scenarios of electrification, clean power and ridership growth to see how an agency's impacts change. Supplemental materials include three fact sheets, key findings, and a PowerPoint presentation with a template for agencies to add their own data. Format and access: a 112-page report (DOI 10.17226/26103) and supplemental files on the National Academies Press page. Licence and cost: free to download; no licence stated on the page read. Caveats: a single base year. The agency-level impacts and scenarios can set transit emission offsets in climate mitigation and capacity planning models. It relates to the National Transit Database and the NBER transit carbon emissions study in the catalogue.
